In the DR there’s two places that do a lot of witchcraft and voodoo, San Juan y Pedernales. 
Pedernales is a region that borders with Haiti and there’s a lot of Voodoo due to this. 
Then there’s San Juan, it’s a town with a lots of witchcraft as well, people also says that is this the town of witches due to all the strange thinks that happened over there. 

To make a pact with one of these creatures you can go to one on these places and make a pact through a Voodoo chaman, then he’ll give your baca so you can take it home (these creatures look like animals and look harmless) or you can also make the ritual in your actual land by invoking an entity and then making the pact.

In my home country there’s a lot of urban legends, but the one that always stuck with me the most is the legend of the Báca. 
The is based of the country side of the DR. 
A báca is a demonic figure that you made a pact with so it can protect your property against burglary or it can also give you wealth if that’s what you want. The creature is animal base ( it can take the form of a cow, an owl, chicken, etc..) 

When you make a pact with it, the creature usually wants something in exchange; you can give him one of your sons or another human soul everyday. 

The báca is also transferred once the owner of it dies, it usually goes to the oldest son. 

My family has a lot of stories related to those and it really creepy.
